Nikhil / Marissa / Sam,

Thanks for the context. I reviewed Helix's comments and prepared narrow counter-language to avoid overly broad publicity carveouts while honoring their confidentiality concerns. High level:

1) Embargo and announcement timing
Proposed: Customer shall provide written notice of any public announcement at least fourteen (14) days prior to publication; Redwood shall not publish case studies or press releases referencing Customer without Customer's prior written consent. However, for product-level release notes and technical blog posts that do not disclose confidential metrics, Redwood may publish after a seven (7) day notice to Customer unless Customer objects in writing.

Reason: preserves Helix's ability to manage PR while not blocking our routine technical comms.

2) Logo and trademark usage
Proposed: Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable right to use Customer's name and logo solely in Redwood's marketing materials, website, customer lists, and sales collateral, subject to Customer's brand guidelines and approval (Customer to respond to approval requests within five (5) business days). Redwood shall not distribute Customer logos to third-party ad networks or resellers without Customer's prior written approval.

3) Quotes & case studies
Proposed: Redwood may request Customer approval for quotes and excerpts; Customer will have thirty (30) days to approve or provide comments. Approval shall not be unreasonably withheld; if Customer provides comments, Redwood may incorporate reasonable edits and circulate for final sign-off.

4) Confidentiality carveout for reference customers
Proposed: Confidential information that is clearly marked or reasonably understood to be confidential shall not be used in public materials, and any aggregated metrics will be anonymized unless Customer consents otherwise.

I attached a redlined order form that implements the above (Helix_OrderForm_redline.pdf). Also including a short SOC2 evidence summary Helix requested. 

If Marissa is comfortable with the timing SLA for approvals (5 business days) I'll present this back to Sam as Redwood's suggested compromise.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
